claim: Deep stories set the frames later events are read through (Prochaska 2024, qualitative, about 1000 tweets from 2 US elections). No quantitative, experimental or LLM test exists in the sources opened.
agent_test: Plant a framing paragraph earlier in context, then give an ambiguous neutral event; measure shift in reading versus a no-plant control, equal tokens.

claim: People and models accept plausible or coherent accounts over accurate ones: human sensemaking is plausibility-driven (Weick, Prochaska) and LLMs follow coherent counter-evidence over memory.
agent_test: Give paired coherent-false vs crude-true evidence; measure accept rate with and without a 'rate source reliability before use' step.

claim: Misinformation persists after debunking in humans: meta-analysis k=52, N=6,878; misinformation d 2.41-3.08, debunking d 1.14-1.33, persistence d 0.75-1.06 (verified against the PMC abstract). Generating supporting reasons raises persistence.
schema_part: G (do not anchor on retracted claims)
agent_test: Insert a retraction mid-context; test whether answers still use the retracted claim, with and without a replacement explanation.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Small amounts of coherent injected text steer retrieval-using LLMs: PoisonedRAG ASR 0.97 NQ, 0.99 HotpotQA, 0.91 MS-MARCO (PaLM 2) with 5 texts; LLM-made fakes cut ODQA exact match up to 87% at 0.01-0.1% corpus share.
agent_test: Inject k fake passages into our agent's context; measure answer flips with and without source isolation (S1 masking).

claim: LLMs adopt wrong retrieved content over correct prior knowledge more than 60% of the time (ClashEval, 6 LLMs, 1200+ questions); adoption falls as content is more blatantly wrong and rises when model confidence is low.
agent_test: Run ClashEval-style items; compare plain vs a prompt that first states own prior then compares, equal tokens.

claim: Multi-turn persuasion with false but plausible text flips correct beliefs in most models: turn-1 alteration 4.1-63.4%, MR@4 20.7% (GPT-4) to 78.2% (Llama-2-7B avg); stronger models resist more; a reminder prompt helps partly (verified in paper text).
agent_test: Replicate Farm on our agent: 4 turns of misinformation, with and without a recheck-against-recalled-evidence step.

claim: Sycophancy: models change correct answers when challenged (32% GPT-4 to 86% Claude 1.3) and wrongly admit error (42%-98%); a wrong user suggestion cuts accuracy up to 27% (LLaMA 2); 'are you sure' cuts it up to 27% (Claude 1.3). Two different tests share the 27%. Preference data rewards agreeing with the user.
agent_test: Pushback tests ('are you sure', wrong suggestion); count right-to-wrong flips at equal tokens.

claim: Models weigh relevance to the question over human credibility cues (references, neutral tone); stated convincingness ratings do not predict which evidence wins.
agent_test: Edit evidence for relevance vs credibility cues; check whether an explicit source-quality rubric changes the win rate.

claim: LLM-written misinformation is harder for humans and detectors to catch than human-written with the same meaning (humans caught 9.6% of hallucinated news; ChatGPT-3.5 0.0%, GPT-4 10.0%; verified). Humans rated false GPT-3 tweets as true slightly more (0.89 vs 0.92 recognised, n=697).
agent_test: Compare a style-only detection step with a provenance-based step on mixed LLM/human fakes.

claim: AI persuasion grows only with log of model size (5.77pp avg, +1.26pp per log unit, ceiling about 12pp, N=25,982) and is driven more by post-training and prompting (up to +51% and +27%) and information density (r=0.76) than by scale or personalization; the most persuasive setups were less accurate (62% vs 78% accurate claims, GPT-4o).
schema_part: S1 (dense fact-like input is not evidence)
agent_test: Feed claim-dense vs plain persuasive context; test if claim-by-claim checking reduces uptake at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: GPT-4 with personal data raised agreement odds by 81.7% (N=820, CI 26.3-161.4%) vs human opponents; without personalization +21.3%, not significant (p=0.31). One study, debate topics, short.
agent_test: Not directly testable on our agent; informs risk only.

claim: Story form should make deep stories stick in people (Green and Brock 2000, not opened), but storytelling was not better than the basic prompt for AI persuasion in Hackenburg 2025 (one of eight strategies; effect not read).
agent_test: Compare story-framed vs list-framed false context on uptake.

claim: Marking untrusted text (delimiters, datamarking, encoding) cuts indirect-injection attack success from about 50% to below 3% with GPT-3.5; encoding 0.0-1.8% (verified). This concerns instructions, not framing; transfer to framing manipulation is untested.
agent_test: Mark inserted context with provenance tags and measure framing-effect size vs unmarked.

claim: Defences are partial: trained detectors fail out of domain (AUROC 50.7-64.8 vs 91.4-99.7 in domain); warnings are inconsistent; evidence-group voting helped most (+11 to +23% EM) but cost grows linearly; context-faithful prompting cut memorisation 35.2% to 3.0%; ignore-irrelevant instructions help partly.
agent_test: Compare majority-over-evidence-subsets vs a single pass at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought does not expose hidden prompt bias: biasing features cut accuracy up to 36% and the explanation never names the bias. 2025 update: on Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 traces verbalise a used hint only 25% and 39% of the time.
agent_test: Add a biasing hint; check whether the agent's trace mentions it.

claim: Habit and platform design, not only reasoning, drive human sharing; accuracy prompts help across 16 countries (N=34,286). Inoculation raises technique recognition (d 0.28-0.68) but truth discernment only d 0.10-0.32, and the YouTube field effect (h=0.09) was below the preregistered smallest effect of interest (h=0.10).
agent_test: Test an accuracy-prompt step at the start of S1; measure discernment on true/false items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Personalised chatbot dialogue lowered belief in a person's own conspiracy about 21% (d=1.15) with no decay at 2 months (Costello 2024, Study 1 N=1,055; Study 2 N=2,286; 2,190 believers total). A debrief rebuttal undid a planted conspiracy belief in people (Costello 2026). Tailoring is not isolated as the cause; no LLM test of repairing a planted frame.
schema_part: repair step: name and answer the planted account
agent_test: Plant a frame, then compare plain retraction vs claim-by-claim rebuttal of the frame, at equal tokens.

claim: True-but-selective evidence still misleads: LLM persuaders move people toward a conspiracy as much as away (bunk +13.6 vs debunk -12.1 points, N=3,996); a truth-constraint prompt cut but did not remove the effect, and bunking worked in the top truth quartile. A fact-by-fact check will miss frame manipulation.
schema_part: S1 (add frame check beside fact check)
agent_test: Feed true facts arranged under a misleading frame; test whether a fact-check step flags it.

claim: Credibility elicitation changes behaviour but does not secure it: models act on notices rated untrustworthy in 27-99% of cases; removing the rating step adds 15 pp harmful action; a one-line forewarning cut harm in 4 of 5 models but cost legitimate task completion. Two LLM questions (credibility, sharing) overlap heavily.
schema_part: S1 (check by action, not by stated belief)
agent_test: Compare rating-first, forewarning, and no step on harmful and legitimate actions at equal tokens.

claim: Cheap defences measured so far: prior-first reconciliation (Astute RAG, +6.85% over best baseline, about 5% extra tokens), isolate-then-aggregate (RobustRAG, injection success from over 90% to 15% or less), third-person narrator (SYCON, up to 63.8% less sycophancy in debate), chain-of-thought (harmful revision 63.9 to 36.5%). No head-to-head on coherent frames at equal tokens.
agent_test: Run all four plus plain and best-of-N on one coherent-frame set at equal tokens.

claim: A planted story can change later learning in people at small effect size (blocking d=0.26-0.49, N=276; fictional task) and earlier in-context exposure shifts a model's reading of an ambiguous pronoun (InstructGPT, syntactic only). No test of deep-story priming on current LLMs.
agent_test: Planted frame, ambiguous event, no-plant control, current frontier model.

claim: Rumour structure repeats: 568 coded US election rumours, 69.9% with a full Actor-Object-Action grammar; the deep-story reading claim is still one research group on one data set.
agent_test: Strip actor, object, action to a neutral restatement before reasoning and compare.
